01 · About

A community joined in prayer and work

In Kybliary, Zakarpattia, community life brings together shared prayer, spiritual guidance and everyday work. The social kitchen and hot meals for travellers and visitors are part of its service. Its documentary history can be traced through the registration records.

Learn more ↗

ISF · Our mission

To sustain a space for prayer and shared life, where faith takes shape in daily work, attentiveness and responsibility for one another.

We seek to bring spiritual life into the ordinary tasks of each day: prayer, care for our shared home, work and personal conversation. For us, community begins with a willingness to be present and to take part in what we do together.

Our mission is to nurture a shared life with room for silence and conversation, personal prayer and collective responsibility. These are the principles we seek to carry into everyday life at the community.

Our values

Principles we seek to follow in prayer, work and our relationships.

01

Prayer

To remain turned towards God amid everyday tasks. To make room for personal and shared prayer, including the evening Rosary.

02

Attentiveness to each person

To listen to one another, respect personal dignity and see more than a person's difficulties. To nurture calm and kind communication.

03

Shared responsibility

To take part in daily duties and the care of our shared home. To notice needs close to us and look after what has been entrusted to the community.

04

Simplicity and mutual support

To recognise the value of ordinary tasks, shared work and time together. To support one another through attention, presence and the contribution each person can make.

The certificate names the Uzhhorod District State Administration of Zakarpattia Region as the registration authority.

The certificate's details were checked against the photograph of the paper document and the register extract. Address and leadership details refer to the dates of those sources; current visiting arrangements are confirmed separately.

Our activities

Prayer, shared work and service to others. Each card introduces an aspect of community life.

1 / 9

Community activity

Shared prayer

Shared prayer brings the community together in turning towards God. It makes room for thanksgiving, requests and remembrance of those who need support.

Prayer teaches trust in God and attentiveness to others. It reminds us that care can begin with a willingness to remember a person before the Lord.

Community activity

Worship

The community’s church provides a place for shared prayer and church life. Worship turns our attention towards Christ and listening to the Word of God.

Gathering before God calls us to repentance, mercy and responsibility for one another. What we hear in church finds expression in our daily actions.

Community activity

Spiritual guidance

Spiritual guidance and ethical formation are areas of the community’s service. Conversation, attentive listening and a Christian understanding of life have a place here.

A sincere word can support a person seeking a responsible decision. Spiritual conversation encourages self-examination without judging others and a willingness to make a personal effort.

Community activity

Work and obedience

Daily work helps care for the home, garden and grounds. Ordinary responsibilities make room for patience, diligence and responsibility.

Obedience is presented here as a willingness to contribute to a shared task. Work gains spiritual meaning when it is understood as service to God and neighbour.

Community activity

Community life

The sisters and novices share prayer, everyday tasks and time for conversation. Shared life is made up of many small acts of attentiveness.

Being present means learning to hear another person and respond to their needs. This closeness recalls the Christian calling to love one’s neighbour in ordinary circumstances.

Community activity

Hospitality

The community presents itself as a home that welcomes an encounter with another person. Hospitality begins with a kind word and respect for the guest’s dignity.

To receive a neighbour is to notice their presence rather than pass by. The Christian meaning of hospitality is found in a simple willingness to give attention.

Community activity

Social kitchen

The social kitchen and a place for hot meals serve travellers and visitors. This care involves the everyday work of the community’s sisters.

A meal can become a simple expression of love for a neighbour. Through food, attention and a shared table, service takes a tangible human form.

Community activity

Ornamental plants

Ornamental plants are among the results of the community’s work. They bring care for living creation together with patient everyday effort.

Caring for a plant teaches attentiveness to life that depends on our care. This work calls for consistency and gratitude for the world entrusted to us.

Community activity

Conversation around the Word of God

Conversation around the Word of God is one of the activities identified by the community. Shared reflection offers a way to consider faith and life thoughtfully.

Listening to the Word also means considering how to respond through our actions. Attentive conversation helps connect what is heard with responsibility for everyday choices.
